sections.h2: Which Marion County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
In Marion County the property appraiser sets values and the tax collector bills and collects, with the clerk of court keeping the records. All three work out of the Ocala area, and each has its own website.

  • Marion County Property Appraiser: parcel and sales search, a property tax estimator, homestead e-filing, TPP return e-filing, a page of important dates and information on the TRIM notice and the Value Adjustment Board. The office lists its address as 501 SE 25th Avenue, Ocala, with walk-ins welcome or appointments available.
  • Marion County Tax Collector: pay taxes online, search the tax roll, apply for a tax deed online, buy county-held certificates, and read about installment plans, deferred taxes and delinquent taxes. The main office is at the McPherson Complex, 503 SE 25th Avenue, Ocala, and the office runs eight locations across the county.
  • Marion County Clerk of Court and Comptroller: the county recorder, the keeper of Official Records, and the office that handles tax deed sales and the Value Adjustment Board.

Keep the roles straight when you call. The appraiser answers questions about value and exemptions. The collector answers questions about what you owe.

sections.h2: When are Marion County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Marion County taxes and assessments are due November 1 and become delinquent April 1, according to the tax collector's payment page. Florida allows a discount for early payment starting in November.

Early payment discounts on the Marion County Tax Collector's payment page
Month paidDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchGross amount, no discount

On or after April 1 the amount you owe depends on the day the collector receives your payment, not the postmark. The office also notes that taxes are payable even if a bill never arrives, and that a mortgage company paying from escrow may request the bill and the owner then gets an informational copy. The collector's notice for 2026 states that the real estate, tangible personal property and railroad rolls opened for collection.

sections.h2: What can Marion County homeowners do about the bill?
sections.html:
Several options exist before a bill turns delinquent. The collector's property tax menu lists an installment plan and deferred taxes, and the state describes the rules behind both.

  • Installment plan: section 197.222 lets owners prepay and pay in installments, with the application due to the tax collector by May 1 of the assessment year.
  • Homestead deferral: Form DR-570 goes to the tax collector by March 31. Deferral covers the portion above 5 percent of last year's household income, and a permanent resident aged 65 or older may defer the part above 3 percent.
  • Partial payments: before the delinquency date these are at the tax collector's discretion under section 197.374.
  • Escrow: a lender holding escrow can request your bill, so check with your servicer before paying twice.

Ask the collector which of these still apply to the parcel you plan to sell, since a plan tied to the current owner may not fit a buyer.

sections.h2: How does Marion County assess and cap property value?
sections.html:
The appraiser assesses all property at just value as of January 1 each year. Exemption and classification applications are due to the appraiser by March 1, and tangible personal property returns by April 1.

Homestead gives up to $50,000 in exemption. The first $25,000 reduces every tax, school taxes included, and the second $25,000 applies to value above $50,000 for non-school taxes only. The state sets the application on Form DR-501 and requires that the home be your permanent residence by January 1.

After the first year, Save Our Homes holds the annual rise in a homestead's assessed value to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change. The state chart shows a cap of 2.7% for 2026. Non-homestead property is limited to a 10 percent increase a year. A sale or other change of ownership resets the parcel to just value the following January 1, with exceptions for transfers between spouses and some transfers at death.

The appraiser's TRIM notice is mailed in August. A value challenge goes to the clerk within 25 days of that notice, and a denied exemption has a 30-day window from the denial letter's mailing.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Marion County taxes?
sections.html:
Unpaid taxes are delinquent from April 1, and the state's revenue department says tax certificates are sold on all unpaid items by June 1. A certificate buyer pays the taxes and earns interest, and the buyer may not contact the owner to demand payment until two years after April 1 of the issue year.

The tax collector's menu gives county owners a path for later stages too: tax deed applications can be made online, and county-held certificates can be bought online. Under section 197.502, a holder can apply for a tax deed once two years have passed since April 1 of the issue year. Notice goes to the titleholder, lienholders and any contract-for-deed buyer, and the opening bid on a homestead includes one-half of the latest assessed value. The clerk's office lists tax deed sales and lands available for taxes among its departments.

An owner who wants to sell should clear the certificate before the deed application stage, since the amount due only grows.

sections.h2: How do you sell a Marion County house with tax owed?
sections.html:
Ask the collector for the exact balance, then have the title company pay it from the sale proceeds at closing. A sale does not require a clean tax record first.

Two state rules touch the closing table. The deed stamp tax is 70 cents on each $100 of consideration under section 201.02, and every party to the deed is liable regardless of which party agrees to pay. The clerk collects it when recording. Separately, a sale restarts the assessment for the next owner at just value, so the buyer's first bill can be higher than yours.

If you inherited the house or fell behind on several years, call the collector for a written payoff before you accept any offer. The Marion County Clerk's Property Alert Service is a free way to be told when a document is recorded against your parcel or name.

faqs.q: Who sends the Marion County property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Marion County Tax Collector sends and collects the bill. The property appraiser sets the value and mails the TRIM notice in August.

faqs.q: When do Marion County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. After that date the amount due depends on when the collector receives your payment, and the postmark does not count.

faqs.q: What is the Marion County early payment discount?
faqs.a: The collector lists 4% for November, 3% for December, 2% for January and 1% for February. March payments pay the gross amount.

faqs.q: Can I apply for homestead exemption in Marion County after March 1?
faqs.a: The state deadline is March 1 of the tax year, filed with the appraiser on Form DR-501. Ask the appraiser's office about any late-filing options for your situation.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay all back taxes before selling in Marion County?
faqs.a: No. The title company can pay a balance from the proceeds. Get a written payoff from the tax collector and confirm whether a certificate has been issued.
